description:
Goal
Make Enum.reduce/3 (and everything built on it) work over a Range with a scalar/tuple accumulator. Today it is completely broken on interp, run, and build.

Current signal
`Enum.reduce(1..3, 0, fn(x, acc) -> acc + x end)` fails on every path:
- interp: `backend executable N expected 2 runtime lane(s), got 3` (backend.rs:1703 lane-count check)
- run / build: panic at native_codegen/driver.rs:971 `debug_assert_eq!(previous, &next)` — one target_fn yields two diverging NativeClosureTargetSurface values (in release the assert vanishes and first-wins silently).

Root cause (isolated by bisection)
The trigger is the conjunction of THREE conditions; remove any one and it works:
1. Source is a Range (List works).
2. Accumulator is a scalar/tuple, i.e. a non-heap-ref `b` (a list/heap-ref accumulator works).
3. The reducer is a capturing closure — which Enum.reduce/3 ALWAYS produces via its bridge lambda `fn(entry, inner_acc) -> {:cont, reducer.(entry, inner_acc)} end` (capturing `reducer`).

Evidence:
- `Enumerable.reduce(Range.new(1,3,1), {:cont, 0}, fn(e,a) -> {:cont, a+e} end)` (non-capturing reducer, called directly) → works ({:done, 6}).
- `Enumerable.reduce(Range.new(1,3,1), {:cont, 0}, fn(e,a) -> {:cont, r.(e,a)} end)` where `r` is captured → FAILS (exec lane 2 vs 3).
- Same capturing wrapper over a List → works.
- `Enum.reduce(list, 0, f)` works; `Enum.reduce(range, [], [_|_])` works (list acc); `Enum.reduce(range, 0, f)` and `Enum.reduce(range, {0,0}, f)` fail.
- Enum.map/Enum.to_list over a Range work (they reduce with a list accumulator).

Interpretation
The capturing reducer closure, threaded through Range's scalar-prefixed recursive reduce_cont/reduce_step (`reduce_cont(first,last,step,current,acc,reducer)` — 4 leading scalar ints vs List's single `list` prefix), acquires two divergent lane/surface shapes for one target body. The tagged-union reduce state `{:cont,b}|{:halt,b}|{:suspend,b}` plus the 2-payload `{:suspended, b, ()->any}` return inflate the expected lane count to 3 when `b` is scalar; a heap-ref `b` masks it behind a uniform ValueRef lane. This is the SAME shared-bridge capture-correlation root cause described in fz-f98, but manifesting as a hard crash over Range rather than a boxing fallback over List.

Relationship to fz-x2n
The native manifestation lands at driver.rs:971 — the same closure-target-surface selection machinery the fz-x2n deterministic_callable_boundary_fallback neighbors. This is the genuine 'one callable value, two diverging ground surfaces' condition fz-x2n's fallback nominally guards, proving (a) the condition IS reachable and (b) the current code crashes on it rather than dispatching. fz-x2n cannot be cleanly resolved while this crashes in the same machinery; hence this blocks fz-x2n.

Required work
- Add a focused fixture: Enum.reduce/3 over a Range with a scalar accumulator (and a tuple-accumulator variant), pinned on interp + run + build.
- Fix the lane/surface accounting so the capturing bridge reducer keeps ONE coherent surface when threaded through Range's scalar-prefixed reduce; do NOT special-case Range — the fix must be generic across the shared Enum.reduce/3 bridge (coordinate with / likely subsumes fz-f98).
- Re-check that the debug_assert at driver.rs:971 is restored to an invariant that genuinely holds (or is replaced by a sound surface reconciliation), not silently bypassed in release.
- Confirm dependent helpers (Enum.reduce/2, each, count/2, reverse over Range, etc.) over Range with scalar accumulators all pass.

Checks
- New Range-reduce scalar-accumulator regression green on all three paths.
- Existing enum_take_drop_split + range_enumerable + map_enumerable matrices remain green.
- cargo test --lib and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings.

comments.text: Additional manifestation: the full enum_tier0 fixture (with reduce/2,3,reduce_while over Range+Map added) fails in release in 0.06s with a fast panic at src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs:2587 'local callable producer reached transport without upstream CallableFlowFact: LocalCallableProducer { function: FunctionId(66), captures: [] }'. Same capture-flow correlation root as the lane mismatch — the shared reduce-bridge closure reaches transport without its upstream CallableFlowFact. Timing note: original enum_tier0 takes 15.00s (release) to hit the fz-hwn.9 drive-limit timeout; the reduce-cluster panics fail far earlier (0.03-0.52s) and currently mask that timeout.

title: Enum.reduce/3 over Range with scalar accumulator crashes on all three paths
